MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 24, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:02 p.m., on May 24, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May, 19, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Legal Counsel: Consideration of Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to
  Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: One Case; Adverse to State of
  California

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

City Council Minutes  1  May 24, 2016
 INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim May through October, 2016, for "Drowning Prevention and Awareness"

  Mayor Ury presented the proclamation to Battalion Chief Ken Harrison.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Judy Bullockus, M.V.: invited the Council Members and residents to Relay for Life which will be
held at Saddleback College from 9:00 a.m. on Saturday, June 4 to 9:00 a.m. on Sunday, June 5,
2016.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: thanked the Voss brothers for bringing a film festival to Mission Viejo. She
said that she hopes the City will continue the festival next year and will hold it at a bigger venue.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 4 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Claim Against the City - Consuelo Gonzalez-Hernandez

  Rejected claim.

5.  Check Register Dated May 6, 2016 in the Amount of $666,004.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  2  May 24, 2016
 6.  Quarterly Check Register Report - Third Quarter of FY 2015-16

  Received and filed.

7.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo – Third Quarter of 2015-16

  Received and filed.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2016

  Received and filed.

10. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2016

  Received and filed.

11. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for March 2016

  Received and filed.

12. Selection of Independent Auditor for Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2016, and June 30,
  2017

  Awarded a contract to Davis Farr LLP to serve as the City's Independent Auditors for the
  Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2016 and June 30, 2017.

13. Provide Pool and Equipment Room Maintenance Services for the Montanoso and
  Sierra Recreation and Fitness Centers, and the Marguerite Aquatics Complex

  Increased Purchase Order 21600137-00 amount by $41,000.00 to One Stop Pool Pros, Inc.
  for fiscal year 2015-2016.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2. City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht asked that her comments be amended in several areas of the Minutes.

City Council Minutes  3  May 24, 2016
   Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to table this matter and
  bring the edited Minutes back for consideration at the next City Council meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

4.  Check Register Dated April 29, 2016 in the Amount of $781,209.45

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Intertech Consultants of Santa
  Clara County for electromagnetic field (EMF) measurements at Flo Jo Park.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that due to the periodic comments that are made about the
  danger of the power lines, the City commissioned an EMF measurement. The results showed
  that the EMF was well within the design specifications for the area and interestingly, the
  report showed that there is more EMF coming from the underground lines than from the lines
  overhead. City Manager Wilberg agreed to send a copy of the report to the City Council
  Members.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report for either of the
  Transportation Corridor Agency boards.

15. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

16. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  4  May 24, 2016
 STAFF REPORTS

17. 115 Trust Agreement Governing the City of Mission Viejo Prefunding Pension
  Obligation Trust

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve Resolution
  16-22 to Adopt the 115 Trust Agreement (A16-15) Governing the City of Mission Viejo
  Prefunding Pension Obligation Trust, effective May 1, 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

18. Possible Refinancing of the Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to adopt
  Resolution 16-23 Directing the Commencement of Proceedings to Refund the Outstanding
  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue Refunding
  Bonds, 2009 Series A, Retaining Consultants in Connection Therewith and Approving
  Official Actions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

19. Capistrano Unified School District Results and Potential Options for Facilities Funding

  Mayor Ury introduced the agenda item.

  The following expressed concern with the proposed $889 million district-wide bond: Judy
  Bullockus, M.V.; Sharon Campbell, M.V.; Wayne Tate, M.V.; Michael Collier, M.V.; and
  Gail Reavis, M.V.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to place this item on the next agenda for
  continued discussion and asked staff to try and coordinate a meeting with Mayor Ury, Mayor
  Pro Tem Bucknum and the Capistrano Unified School District staff. Further, as new

City Council Minutes  5  May 24, 2016
   information becomes available, staff should share it with those who have inquired and
  include it in the agenda materials for June 14, 2016.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:22 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:37 p.m.
with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum was absent.)

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths discussed his attendance at a ribbon cutting ceremony for Tropical
Smoothie where the new business gave its first 100 customers a free smoothie once a week for a
year. He reminded residents of the Rotary Club’s Texas Hold 'Em which will be held on June 11,
2016, at the Murray Community Center. The cost is $60 for dinner and entertainment and $50 of
that fee will go to the charity of the player's choice. Council Member Raths discussed the policy
that the City Council recently passed regarding political signage in restricted areas. He noted that
candidates had to pay a $240 fee and he asked the City Clerk if all of the candidates had paid. City
Clerk Karen Hamman responded that three candidates have paid the fee and all of the major
candidates were notified of the policy. Council Member Raths reminded residents to vote in the
primary election on June 7 and to practice due diligence in evaluating the candidates.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that the Governor has put forward a By Right Housing Proposal
which will basically take away local control regarding zoning for housing and commercial
projects. The bill would trump local authority and he asked that the Mayor send a letter of
opposition to the Governor to express the City’s opposition. Council Member Sachs noted that
when he and Council Member Raths were walking precincts before they were elected, he learned
that a lot of residents don’t know what is going on in the City. He has recommended that staff host
quarterly “Meet Your City Officials” events and the first one will be held on Wednesday, May 25
from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m. in the Plaza Del Lago parking lot near the lake. He encouraged residents
to attend and visit the departmental booths to ask whatever questions they have.

City Council Minutes  6  May 24, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

21. Civic Core Area Vision Plan Process: Concerns as to Process and Scope of Land-use
  Planning/Regulation

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report and expressed her concern with the style of
  polling that consultant SWA is charged to do.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed concern with the notion of mixed-use housing in the Village
  Center.

Council Member Schlicht stated that she is on the ballot for the June 7 election and her signs are
being picked up or stolen. She reminded residents that removing campaign signs is illegal and is
considered petty theft. She asked anyone who sees such activity to please report it or take a picture
of the culprit. She further wondered if it was a coincidence that her signs started disappearing after
a recent controversial agenda item when she addressed her concerns about special interest
influence in the City. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from
Thomas Jefferson: “To compel a man to furnish contributions of money for the propagation of
opinions which he disbelieves is sinful and tyrannical.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury told Council member Schlicht that her colleagues’ response to her agenda item was
not actually a response, it was a rebuttal. He reminded residents that the City’s Memorial Day
ceremony will be held on Monday, May 30 at 8:30 a.m. and he encouraged everyone to attend.
Mayor Ury announced that he had the pleasure of embarking on an aircraft carrier for an overnight
trip 100 miles out to sea. He stated that it was an amazing opportunity and he thanked the Navy
personnel and everyone else who helped set it up.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:38 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Laguna Niguel City Council Member Jerry
McCloskey, to Tuesday, June 14, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 14, 2016

City Council Minutes  7  May 24, 2016
